E25_finding: 13 duplicate-session-ID questions; semantic equality not yet checked by specialist.

callpaths.finding: Historical loader retains each source session occurrence in a list, but turn IDs use session ID plus turn position. Ranking score/date maps key by those aliases, merging repeated identities; final target list can retain repeated aliases. No source-index disambiguation.

Ranking validation dict(zip(...)) retains the final session for each duplicate ID. official_prompt independently overwrites by_id and dates in source order, then resolves all ranked turns and preopen predecessors against that final occurrence. seen keys use (sid,turn), so duplicate source occurrences cannot be distinguished. This is verified static behavior; actual payload loss depends on source equality counter.

rounds_for uses physical session/turn indexes to generate opaque source/session identities and preserves occurrences. The historical reference adapter still assigns aliases[tid] with last-write semantics. Current role-aware occurrence preservation must not be conflated with historical preopen rendering.

_groups_for_question accumulates repeated legacy aliases into lists and assigns source handles from qid,session_index,turn_index; preserves separate physical occurrences. This is an existing equivalent to reuse before designing an identity repair.

acceptance: Check all repeated occurrences, canonical full payload, annotation-stripped role/content, exact dates, winner/shadowed indexes, top30 reference membership, persistent21 membership and E25 duplicate set equality. Different dates or reader payload reject lossless legacy identity; equal payload/date only establishes content equivalence, not a unique physical identity.
risk: Duplicate IDs cannot alone establish a gold-key contradiction, historical score impact, or completeness of the actual truncated reader prompt.
interpretation: All thirteen groups have equivalent reader role/content but different observation dates. Legacy last-write lookup discards earlier timestamped occurrences, so lossless temporal identity is rejected. One historical top30 ranking touches a repeated alias; no persistent21 case overlaps. Neither answer changes nor historical score impact are established.
